checkpoints.note: By this dispatch the input blob has already been accepted as a face and execution has entered `post`-table glyph-name handling, the subsystem that later performs the failing reverse lookup.

This call asks HarfBuzz to materialize the queried glyph name into the local 5-byte stack buffer `buf`; on the witnessed path the next line reuses that same populated buffer as the vulnerable search key.

checkpoints.code: const uint16_t *gid = (const uint16_t *) hb_bsearch_r (&st, gids, count, sizeof (gids[0]), cmp_key, (void *) this);
checkpoints.note: The fix changes only this call site: it adds `hb_addressof()` and passes `hb_addressof (st)` so `cmp_key()` receives a real `hb_bytes_t*` rather than the caller's stack buffer.
